notes: Each case is the work items as one reader is given them, in the order given, all Relations with supertype Work item in the world below, and a want worked by hand from the page's rules 1, 5, 7 and 8.

world: the world the work items sit in: its id, its Characters, and others, the ids of every other element of it the reader holds. A value written as no id in either list names no element the reader holds. x_packet_source names the same world, as a folder (server null), except where an item's elements are the source_world's.

source_world: another world, the source of the packets that name its elements, whose elements the reader holds too, having resolved those packets there (rule 2); its Characters are no Characters of the world the items sit in.

state_cases want: states, for each item its state, the word `open`, `taken`, `done` or `standing` matched trimmed and without regard to case as the room profile defines it, or null for no state (rule 5); shown, every item (no item is hidden for its state); open_work, for each element any item names in x_packet_elements, the ids of the open work that names it (the items whose state is `open` or `taken`); elements, where present, an item's elements in x_packet_elements' order (rules 1 and 7).

asker_cases want: askers, for each item the Character id x_packet_from names or null (rule 8); lints, each {kind, item}, the one kind `asker`, for a key that is not one id (not a string, or a string empty once trimmed of White_Space as the room profile trims) or that is, written exactly so, an id in others or in the source_world (absent, null and a value that names no element the reader holds, in any spelling, are no lint); waiting_on, for each Character of the world, the ids of the open work whose asker is that Character.

Order: the page orders no list of work items, so shown, each list in open_work, each list in waiting_on, and lints compare as sets, written here in the order the items are given. Only elements is a list in order, x_packet_elements' order (rule 1). states and askers compare as maps.
created_by holds a maker's id, which is no Character of the world. A case's note is prose for the reader of the fixture, never an input.

state_cases.name: standing-is-not-open-work
state_cases.note: A standing item is shown as itself and is open work on none of the elements it names.

state_cases.name: standing-with-a-capital-and-a-trailing-space
state_cases.note: The state is matched trimmed and without regard to case: `Standing ` is `standing`.

state_cases.name: open-taken-and-done-beside-a-standing-item
state_cases.note: The three states read as before; the open and the taken item are open work on the element they share, the done and the standing item are not.

state_cases.name: a-standing-item-keeps-the-packets-order
state_cases.note: Five elements, given in no sorted order: the reader shows them in the order of x_packet_elements.

state_cases.name: elements-are-compared-on-the-items-the-want-names
state_cases.note: Two items; the want carries elements for the standing one only. A reader shows every item's elements, and only the standing item's are compared, in x_packet_elements' order.

state_cases.name: a-subtype-none-of-the-four-is-no-state
state_cases.note: `blocked` is no state: the item is shown and is no open work; the open item beside it is.

state_cases.name: an-empty-or-absent-subtype-is-no-state
state_cases.note: No subtype, a null one, an empty string and spaces alone are none of the four: each is shown and none is open work.

state_cases.name: a-state-followed-by-a-unit-separator
state_cases.note: U+001F is no White_Space, so the room profile's trim leaves it: `open` followed by it is none of the four, no state. A language's trim that strips control characters reads `open`.

state_cases.name: a-byte-order-mark-is-not-trimmed
state_cases.note: U+FEFF is no White_Space, so the room profile's trim leaves it, as its own fixture's byte-order-mark case does: `open` after it is none of the four, no state. A trim that strips U+FEFF reads `open`.

state_cases.name: the-long-s-folds
state_cases.note: The long s (U+017F) folds to s by simple case folding, as the room profile's own fixture folds it: the word is `standing`. Lower-casing leaves the long s, and reads no state.

asker_cases.name: the-asker-is-the-character-the-key-names
asker_cases.note: The asker is the key's Character, not the maker and not actor.

asker_cases.name: no-key-names-no-asker
asker_cases.note: Without the key, or with it null, nobody is the asker and there is no lint: neither the maker in created_by, nor the tool in x_packet_producer, nor actor.

asker_cases.name: a-key-that-is-no-character-names-no-asker
asker_cases.note: The id of a Location the reader holds, an empty string and a list: no asker, each with a lint, never guessed at.

asker_cases.name: an-asker-the-reader-cannot-name
asker_cases.note: An id the reader holds no element for (deleted, hidden from this reader, not served): no asker shown, no lint, never a guess.

asker_cases.name: an-asker-in-upper-case-names-nothing
asker_cases.note: Read as written: the first Character's id in upper case is a spelling no element's own id is written in, so it names nothing the reader holds: no asker, no lint.

asker_cases.name: a-character-whose-own-id-is-in-upper-case
asker_cases.note: The fourth Character's own id is written in upper case. The first item writes it exactly so and names that Character as its asker; the second writes it in lowercase, a spelling no element's own id is written in, so it names nothing the reader holds: no asker, no lint.

asker_cases.name: an-asker-with-a-space-names-nothing
asker_cases.note: Read as written: the first Character's id with a space after it is a spelling no element's own id is written in, so it names nothing the reader holds: no asker, no lint. The key is trimmed only to find whether it is empty.

asker_cases.name: an-asker-that-is-a-number-is-no-id
asker_cases.note: A number is not one id: no asker, with a lint, never read as absent.

asker_cases.name: an-asker-of-white-space-alone-is-no-id
asker_cases.note: An ideographic space, a space and a tab are White_Space alone: empty once trimmed as the room profile trims, the key reads as an empty string does, not one id: no asker, with a lint.

asker_cases.name: an-asker-of-a-unit-separator-alone-names-nothing
asker_cases.note: U+001F alone is no White_Space, so the room profile's trim leaves it and the key is not empty: a string that names nothing the reader holds, no asker, no lint. A language's trim that strips control characters reads it as empty.

asker_cases.name: a-word-that-is-no-id-names-nothing
asker_cases.note: A non-empty string not written in an id's form is still a string: it names nothing the reader holds, no asker, no lint.

asker_cases.name: the-asker-is-of-the-world-the-item-sits-in
asker_cases.note: Both items sit in the world below and are about another world, the source. The asker is read among this world's Characters: the first Character asks the first item; the second names a Character of the source world only, which is no Character of this world, so no asker, with a lint.

asker_cases.name: what-am-i-waiting-on
asker_cases.note: The open and taken items each Character asked for; a done, a standing and an item of no state are no waiting.
